hypothesis: With no prior experiment history and stability already solved, the two most impactful naturalness levers that appear undertested are: (1) gait phase regularity is enforced only moderately (weight -1.0), likely leaving gait_air_cv and gait_contact_cv elevated; and (2) limb symmetry is weighted almost entirely on position (1.0) vs velocity (0.1), which risks a "mirror-pose limp" — legs holding identical shapes but desynchronised in motion. Doubling gait_phase_regularity weight to -2.0 should tighten CV metrics directly. Raising limb_symmetry_velocity_weight from 0.1 to 0.5 addresses the velocity-asymmetry blind spot without touching the overall symmetry weight, keeping the change interpretable. Expected trade-off: linear velocity tracking reward may drop slightly (~5-10%) as the policy reallocates learning capacity toward rhythm and symmetry — this is acceptable and predicted by domain rule #6.
expected_effects: gait_air_cv_mean decreases (more regular swing durations — target below 0.3)
symmetry_vel_cost_mean decreases (better velocity synchronisation between legs)
track_linear_velocity reward decreases slightly (~5-10%) as policy reallocates capacity — acceptable side effect per rule #6
symmetry_pos_cost_mean remains roughly unchanged (position symmetry weight untouched)
